framework: CEFR-inspired Pre-A1, A1, A2, B1, B2 pathways. Practice levels are estimates, not official certifications.

mastery_algorithm.promotion: Advance after at least 80% on two separate attempts plus a short real-life response; otherwise simplify and retry.

levels.name: Starter
levels.goal: Use familiar words and short phrases

levels.name: Elementary Plus
levels.goal: Describe experiences and manage routine tasks

practice_modes.ai_chat: One question at a time; natural conversation; correct one or two high-value errors.
practice_modes.grammar: Quick diagnostic → simple explanation → examples → practice → check.
practice_modes.vocabulary: Meaning → example → common word partner → learner-created sentence → spaced recall.
practice_modes.listening: When audio is available: listen for main idea, answer detail questions, then review transcript.
practice_modes.pronunciation: Only score speech if microphone/audio processing is integrated; never pretend text chat can assess pronunciation.
practice_modes.writing: Show corrected version, explain key changes, then invite a second attempt.

sample_lesson.title: Introduce yourself confidently
sample_lesson.objective: Say your name and where you are from, and ask another person's name.

phrases.bn: আপনার সঙ্গে পরিচিত হয়ে ভালো লাগল।

common_mistakes.better: My name is Riya. / I'm Riya.
common_mistakes.why: Use 'My name is...' or 'I'm...' for a normal introduction.

quiz.q: Introduce yourself in two short English sentences.

daily_tips: Practise a little every day instead of waiting to feel perfect.
Learn phrases in context, not only isolated translations.
Try to recall an answer before revealing hints.
Review difficult words across multiple days rather than cramming.
When audio is available, listen, pause, repeat, and compare.
Aim to be understood first; improve accuracy gradually.
Track recurring mistakes and revisit them.
Practise real goals: introductions, work, school, shopping, travel and interviews.
ai_tutor_system_prompt: You are Speakora AI, a patient practical English coach for learners who may prefer Hindi or Bengali explanations. Use clear natural English suited to the learner's estimated level. Ask one question at a time and encourage the learner to create their own sentences. When correcting, show their sentence, a natural correction, one simple explanation in their selected support language, and one new example. Correct only one or two important errors per turn unless detailed correction is requested. During role-play, stay in character and summarize corrections after the scene. Never claim to hear or score pronunciation unless audio input is actually available. Never claim an official CEFR level or certificate. Be supportive and never mock accents.

research.finding: Organize courses around practical can-do outcomes and multiple language skills.
research.source: Council of Europe CEFR Companion Volume

research.finding: Use level-organized short grammar lessons with practice and checking; little-and-often practice is encouraged.
Spaced practice supports second-language learning; vocabulary benefits when review is paired with retrieval and meaningful use.
